content: If you are unable to swallow lansoprazole capsules, you may open them and sprinkle the contents onto one tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Consume the mixture immediately. Do not mix the contents with any other food. If lansoprazole is administered through a nasogastric (NG) tube, your healthcare provider will provide specific instructions on how to do so properly. Lansoprazole SoluTabs contain phenylalanine, a component of aspartame. Individuals under one year of age may be at a higher risk of experiencing certain side effects from lansoprazole. If your child is under one year old, consult your healthcare provider to discuss the potential risks. Before using lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any prescription or over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or other supplements you are taking. This information will help your provider determine if lansoprazole is appropriate for you. If you have any of the following conditions, notify your healthcare provider: low blood potassium levels (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium levels (hypocalcemia), low blood sodium levels (hyponatremia), liver problems, or phenylketonuria. Lansoprazole may interact with other medications and supplements. Before starting lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about any prescription or OTC medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or other supplements you are using. Specific medications to discuss include methotrexate, digoxin (used for irregular heartbeat and some types of heart failure), warfarin (a blood thinner), theophylline (used for certain lung diseases), clarithromycin (an antibiotic for infections), tacrolimus (used to prevent organ transplant rejection), certain antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir for HIV/AIDS), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin (used for tuberculosis). Some medications may alter the blood levels of lansoprazole, and vice versa. Always provide a complete list of medications you are taking or have recently taken to your healthcare provider. The effects of lansoprazole on pregnancy or an unborn baby are not well understood. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. They will advise you on whether you should take lansoprazole during pregnancy. Do not take lansoprazole while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Take lansoprazole before meals. It is unknown whether alcohol consumption affects lansoprazole. Always inform your healthcare provider about any medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using, as lansoprazole may affect the absorption of certain medications. If you or someone else has taken too much lansoprazole, seek medical attention immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of lansoprazole, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most current and personalized guidance.
